title: Karina
lead: The website of Karina — the Istanbul and Bodrum home of Azimut Yachts and Williams Jet Tenders. I built the whole site single-handedly, powered end to end by the COST admin panel.

hero.alt: Karina homepage: video hero of a yacht at sea under the Karina logo

sections.title: A showroom for yachts, online
paragraphs: Karina sells new Azimut yachts, Williams jet tenders and pre-owned boats from offices in Istanbul and Bodrum. The site has to feel as premium as the boats — big imagery, video and calm typography — while staying fast and easy for search engines to index.

I built the entire site on my own in Next.js and TypeScript: the brand and model pages, the new and used yacht catalogs, detailed listing pages with full specifications, news, and the English / Turkish versions — plus its CI/CD pipeline and code-quality rules.

sections.title: Every word and photo comes from COST
sections.intro: The Karina team doesn't touch code to update the site. Yachts, models, specifications, prices, galleries, PDFs, second-hand listings and news are all managed in the COST admin panel — which I also built — and the website renders whatever is published there.

note.text: Both ends are mine: the panel where content is entered, and the site where it's shown. See

items.label: SEO
items.title: Built to be found
items.text: Next.js pages with their own titles and descriptions for every brand, model and listing, so each yacht can rank on its own.

items.label: CONTENT
items.title: Driven by the admin panel
items.text: Prices, specs, galleries, PDFs and news come from COST, so the sales team updates the site without a developer.

items.label: MEDIA
items.title: Rich, but light
items.text: Video heroes, sliders and large galleries, with optimized images so heavy media doesn't slow the page down.

items.label: DELIVERY
items.title: CI/CD from day one
items.text: GitHub Actions pipeline, plus ESLint, Prettier and Husky pre-commit hooks keeping the codebase consistent.
